quests.instruction: It grows in hanging clusters on a palm, is sweet and sticky, and has one long pit. Which fruit fits all three clues?
quests.hint: Check each clue. Two of these fail at least one.
quests.explanation: Date fits all three. Fig grows on a tree and has tiny seeds, and olive is not sweet and sticky.
quests.funFact: Dates are among the oldest fruits that people have grown.

quests.instruction: It grows on low vines in wet fields, tastes very tart and bounces when fresh. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think about a bog.
quests.explanation: Cranberry fits all three. Cherries grow on trees, and strawberries are not tart bog fruits that bounce.
quests.funFact: Cranberries are native to North America.

quests.instruction: It grows on flat cactus pads, has tiny spines and is sweet inside. Which fruit fits all three clues?
quests.hint: Only one of these has flat pads.
quests.explanation: Prickly pear fits all three. Dragon fruit also grows on a cactus but has scales, and mulberry grows on a tree.
quests.funFact: The fruit of the prickly pear is called tuna in some places.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both keep ripening after they are picked?
quests.hint: Remember which fruits do not ripen after picking.
quests.explanation: Bananas and avocados keep ripening off the plant. Strawberries, grapes, cherries and blueberries are best picked ripe.
quests.funFact: Many fruits that ripen after picking give off a natural gas called ethylene.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both have a hollow middle with seeds?
quests.hint: Think about what you scoop out before eating.
quests.explanation: Papaya and melon have hollow middles full of seeds. Mango and peach have stones, and apple and pear have cores.
quests.funFact: Melons and papayas are often scooped with a spoon.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits belong to the rose family?
quests.hint: Think about fruits that grow in cooler places.
quests.explanation: Apples and strawberries are both in the rose family. Bananas, pineapples, mangoes and papayas are tropical fruits from other families.
quests.funFact: Roses, apples and strawberries all have flowers with five petals.

quests.instruction: Which is the safest choice for a toddler's snack?
quests.hint: Think about size, shape and hard pieces.
quests.explanation: Soft banana slices are easy to chew. Whole grapes and cherries with pits can block a small child's throat.
quests.funFact: Bananas are soft, so they are a favorite first fruit for babies.

quests.instruction: A recipe needs a very sour juice to brighten the dish. Which fruit fits best?
quests.hint: Think about a sharp, tangy taste.
quests.explanation: Lime juice is very sour and tangy. Banana and melon are mild and sweet.
quests.funFact: A little lime juice can brighten soups, salads and drinks.

quests.instruction: Which fruit keeps its shape best when baked in a pie?
quests.hint: Think about firmness.
quests.explanation: Firm apples hold their shape when baked, while bananas and raspberries turn soft or fall apart.
quests.funFact: Firm, tart apples are favorites for baking.

quests.instruction: Which statement is true for both bananas and plantains?
quests.correctAnswer: They grow in hands on tall plants
options: They grow in hands on tall plants
They have a hard pit in the center
quests.hint: Think about how each grows.
quests.explanation: Bananas and plantains both grow in hands on tall plants.
quests.funFact: Plantains and bananas are close relatives.

quests.instruction: What do lemons and limes have in common?
quests.correctAnswer: They are citrus fruits with sour juice
options: They grow on vines near the ground
They have a core full of seeds
They are citrus fruits with sour juice
quests.hint: Think about their family and their taste.
quests.explanation: Lemons and limes are both citrus fruits with sour juice.
quests.funFact: Lemon and lime trees both like warm weather.

quests.instruction: What do cherries and plums share?
quests.correctAnswer: They have one hard pit and grow on trees
options: They have one hard pit and grow on trees
They grow in bunches on vines
They have a core with several seeds
quests.hint: Think about their centers and where they grow.
quests.explanation: Cherries and plums both grow on trees and have one hard pit.
quests.funFact: Cherries and plums are both related to peaches and apricots.

quests.instruction: Scientists say that only one of these is a true berry. Which one?
quests.hint: Scientists look at how the fruit forms from the flower.
quests.explanation: A true berry develops from one flower and has seeds inside soft flesh. Bananas fit, while strawberries and raspberries form differently.
quests.funFact: Grapes, tomatoes and avocados are true berries too.

quests.instruction: Why is a pineapple covered in diamond-shaped eyes?
quests.correctAnswer: Each eye grew from a flower that joined the others
options: Each eye is a leaf that dried and curled up
Each eye is a seed that pushed through the skin
Each eye grew from a flower that joined the others
quests.hint: Remember that a pineapple is made of many small parts.
quests.explanation: A pineapple forms from many small flowers that grow together, and each eye marks one of them.
quests.funFact: A pineapple plant flowers all at once, and the fruits join into one.

quests.instruction: Each tiny dot on a strawberry is actually what?
quests.correctAnswer: A tiny fruit holding a seed
options: A speck of dirt stuck to the skin
A tiny fruit holding a seed
A drop of dried sugar on the skin
quests.hint: Look closely at the surface.
quests.explanation: Each dot is a very small fruit that holds one seed, which is why a strawberry has seeds on the outside.
quests.funFact: A single strawberry has about two hundred of these tiny fruits.

quests.instruction: Why can jam be kept for a long time?
quests.correctAnswer: Cooking with sugar helps stop it from spoiling quickly
options: Cooking with sugar helps stop it from spoiling quickly
It is kept frozen all the way from the farm to the shelf
It contains no water and no sugar of any kind
quests.hint: Think about what is added when jam is made.
quests.explanation: Cooking fruit with sugar, and sealing it in a jar, helps stop jam from spoiling quickly.
quests.funFact: Sealed jars also keep air out.

quests.instruction: Why are some fruits dried in the sun?
quests.correctAnswer: Removing water helps them keep longer
options: Removing water helps them keep longer
The sun adds extra water to the fruit
The sun makes the fruit grow bigger inside
quests.hint: Think about what spoils fruit.
quests.explanation: Drying removes water, and without water, spoilage germs cannot grow easily, so dried fruit keeps longer.
quests.funFact: Raisins, dried apricots and dried figs are traditionally sun-dried in many places.

quests.instruction: Why are canned fruits heated?
quests.correctAnswer: Heating kills germs and sealing keeps new ones out
options: Heating makes the fruit grow riper and sweeter
Sealing freezes the fruit solid inside the can
Heating kills germs and sealing keeps new ones out
quests.hint: Think about keeping germs away.
quests.explanation: Canning heats the fruit to kill germs and then seals the can so new germs cannot get in.
quests.funFact: Canning was invented to help keep food for sailors and soldiers.

quests.instruction: Two oranges look the same size. One feels heavy with thin skin, and one feels light with thick skin. Which will probably give more juice?
quests.hint: Think about weight and flesh.
quests.explanation: A heavy orange usually holds more juice, and thin skin means there is more flesh.
quests.funFact: Some oranges are bred especially for juicing.

quests.instruction: You are serving watermelon to 20 guests, including little children. Which choice is easiest?
quests.hint: Think about what makes eating easier.
quests.explanation: Seedless watermelon is easy to eat because there are no big seeds to pick out.
quests.funFact: Seedless watermelons became popular in the late 1900s.

quests.instruction: You want bananas to eat in four days. One bunch is green and one is yellow with brown spots. Which bunch is the better choice?
quests.hint: Think about how bananas change over time.
quests.explanation: Green bananas will ripen over the next few days, while spotted ones will be too ripe by then.
quests.funFact: Hanging bananas on a hook can keep them from bruising.

quests.instruction: It is not red. It has no pit. It grows in bunches. It is eaten with its skin on. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Cross out each fruit that breaks a clue.
quests.explanation: Grapes fit every clue. Cherries are red with a pit, and bananas are peeled.
quests.funFact: A bunch of grapes is sometimes called a cluster.

quests.instruction: It is not round. It is not eaten with its skin. It grows in hands. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Cross out the round fruits first.
quests.explanation: Banana fits every clue. Orange and apple are round, and apple is eaten with its skin.
quests.funFact: A hand of bananas can have between ten and twenty bananas.

quests.instruction: It grows on a vine, has no pit and its skin is not eaten. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Cross out the fruits that break a clue.
quests.explanation: Passion fruit fits every clue. Grapes are eaten with their skin, and plums grow on trees and have pits.
quests.funFact: Passion fruit vines love warm, sunny spots.

quests.instruction: All citrus fruits have juicy segments. A lime is a citrus fruit. What must be true?
options: A lime has a hard pit
A lime grows on a vine
quests.hint: Follow the clues one step at a time.
quests.explanation: If every citrus fruit has juicy segments and a lime is citrus, then a lime must have juicy segments.
quests.funFact: This kind of careful thinking is called logic.

quests.instruction: No melon has a hard pit. A peach has a hard pit. What must be true?
quests.correctAnswer: A peach is not a melon
options: A peach is not a melon
quests.hint: Think about what a peach has that melons do not.
quests.explanation: Since melons have no hard pit and a peach does, a peach cannot be a melon.
quests.funFact: Sorting fruits into groups is called classifying.

quests.instruction: Some fruits grow on vines. Grapes grow on vines. Does that mean every vine fruit is a grape?
quests.correctAnswer: No, other fruits like kiwi also grow on vines
options: No, other fruits like kiwi also grow on vines
Yes, all fruits that grow on vines are grapes
Yes, because only grapes can grow on vines
quests.hint: Be careful about jumping to conclusions.
quests.explanation: Grapes are one of many vine fruits, and kiwi, passion fruit and melons also grow on vines.
quests.funFact: Careful thinking avoids jumping to conclusions.

quests.instruction: You need a fruit that is sturdy, needs no fridge, peels easily by hand and is loved by kids. Which fits best?
quests.hint: Think about a snack that survives a school bag.
quests.explanation: Mandarins are sturdy, peel easily by hand and do not need a fridge. Strawberries and cut melon are delicate.
quests.funFact: Mandarins are a popular lunchbox fruit in many countries.

quests.instruction: Two kids want to share one mango equally. What is the fairest and safest plan?
quests.correctAnswer: A grown-up cuts off the two cheeks, one for each
options: One child eats the whole mango while the other waits
Each child takes bites from the same mango
A grown-up cuts off the two cheeks, one for each
quests.hint: Think about fair shares and the knife.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can cut off the two wide cheeks of a mango, so each child gets an equal share safely.
quests.funFact: Mango cheeks can be scored into squares and eaten with a spoon.

quests.instruction: A shopper compares two pineapples. One smells sweet at the base and one has no smell. Which is the better choice?
quests.correctAnswer: The one that smells sweet at the base
options: The one that smells sweet at the base
The one with no smell and a hard base
Either, because smell does not matter
quests.hint: Remember the smell clue.
quests.explanation: A sweet smell at the base is a good sign of a ripe pineapple.
quests.funFact: A fresh pineapple's crown leaves should look green and healthy.
